name: New Bedford
note_en: This is where Ishmael waits for a whaling ship at the start of Moby-Dick. The Seamen's Bethel, the chapel where he hears Father Mapple's sermon, is still here, and in 1961 it added a pulpit shaped like a ship's bow to match the book. Melville knew the place firsthand: in 1841 he shipped out on a whaler from Fairhaven, just across the harbor
note: 《白鲸》里以实玛利出海前落脚的捕鲸城。他去听梅普尔神父布道的捕鲸人教堂（Seamen's Bethel）至今还在，船头形状的讲坛是 1961 年照小说添上的。梅尔维尔本人 1841 年就是从这里对岸的费尔黑文登上捕鲸船的

name: Nantucket
note_en: The Pequod sails from Nantucket, and Melville writes about the island as the center of the whaling world. The funny thing is that he hadn't been here yet. His first visit was in 1852, a year after the book came out. Today the Whaling Museum brings that world back to life
note: 裴廓德号的母港。梅尔维尔把这座岛写成捕鲸业的世界中心，可他写书时还没来过——直到《白鲸》出版后的 1852 年才第一次上岛。岛上的捕鲸博物馆讲的正是书里那个世界

name: Walden Pond
note_en: Thoreau moved into a one-room cabin he'd built on the north shore on July 4, 1845, and stayed two years, two months, and two days. Walden came out of that experiment. The cabin is long gone, but stone posts mark where it stood, and visitors still add rocks to the cairn beside it. There's a replica of the cabin near the parking lot
note: 梭罗 1845 年 7 月 4 日搬进湖边自己盖的小木屋，住了两年两个月零两天，写成《瓦尔登湖》。木屋原址在北岸林中，立着石柱，旁边是一堆访客一块块添上去的石头；停车场边有一座照原样复建的小屋

name: Washington, D.C.
note_en: Whitman spent most of the Civil War in Washington. By day he worked as a government clerk; the rest of his time he spent in the army hospitals, sitting with wounded soldiers, writing letters home for them, and bringing small gifts of candy and spare change. His notes from those wards became some of the most moving pages in Specimen Days
note: 南北战争期间惠特曼在这里当政府文员，业余时间几乎都在各家战地医院里：给伤兵读书、代写家信、送零钱和糖果。《典型的日子》里那些病房记录，就是他在这座城里一天天写下的

name: Falmouth
note_en: In December 1862 Whitman spotted his brother George's name on a casualty list and rushed to the front at Fredericksburg. He found George, only lightly wounded, near a brick mansion on the Rappahannock that had been turned into a field hospital. Under a tree outside lay a pile of amputated arms and legs. That sight changed Whitman's life and sent him into the hospitals. The house is Chatham Manor, now part of a national military park
note: 1862 年 12 月，惠特曼在伤亡名单上看到弟弟乔治的名字，一路找到弗雷德里克斯堡前线。他在拉帕汉诺克河岸一座砖砌宅邸里找到了弟弟，门外树下堆着截下来的手脚——这一幕让他从此投身战地护理。那座宅邸就是查塔姆庄园，现属国家军事公园，可以参观

name: Camden
note_en: Whitman spent his last years in a modest house on Mickle Street, the only home he ever owned. He lived there until he died in 1892, still revising Leaves of Grass right to the end. The house is now a museum, and the granite tomb he designed for himself is in Harleigh Cemetery across town
note: 惠特曼晚年的家。米克尔街上那座小楼是他一生唯一买下的房子，他在这里住到 1892 年去世，不断修订《草叶集》；故居现为博物馆。他自己设计的花岗岩墓就在城里的哈利公墓

name: Pittsburgh
note_en: In 1879, at age sixty, Whitman finally took his first trip out West, and Pittsburgh was one of his stops along the way. In Specimen Days he describes the steel city at night, with its furnace fires, its smoke, and its lights reflected on the rivers
note: 1879 年惠特曼六十岁，第一次西行到大平原，途经这座炼钢城。《典型的日子》记下了他眼里夜晚的匹兹堡：火光、浓烟和河上的灯

name: Orchard House
prototype_of: 《小妇人》马奇家的原型：奥尔科特一家 1858 至 1877 年住在这里。1868 年路易莎就在父亲为她做的那块半月形窗间书桌上写成了《小妇人》，书桌和梅（小说里的艾米）在墙上画的画都还在
prototype_of_en: The Marches' house in Little Women is based on this one. The Alcotts lived here from 1858 to 1877, and in 1868 Louisa wrote the novel at a little half-moon desk her father built for her between two windows. The desk is still there, along with drawings her sister May (the real Amy) sketched right on the walls

name: Great Neck
prototype_of: 《了不起的盖茨比》里西卵的原型：菲茨杰拉德 1922 至 1924 年租住在大颈镇，在这里开始构思这部小说。隔着曼哈塞特湾对岸的桑兹角，就是黛西住的东卵
prototype_of_en: Great Neck is the real West Egg. Fitzgerald rented a house here from 1922 to 1924 and started The Great Gatsby while living in town. Across Manhasset Bay is Sands Point, the model for Daisy's East Egg

name: The Plaza Hotel
note_en: Two big moments in The Great Gatsby happen at the Plaza. Jordan tells Nick the story of Daisy and Gatsby over tea here, and later, on the hottest day of the summer, everyone crowds into a suite upstairs, where Tom finally confronts Gatsby. The Fitzgeralds were regulars at the hotel themselves
note: 《了不起的盖茨比》两场关键戏都在这家饭店：乔丹在茶园里向尼克讲出黛西和盖茨比的往事；第七章那个酷热的下午，几个人挤进饭店套房，汤姆当众戳穿盖茨比。菲茨杰拉德夫妇本人也是这里的常客

name: Sullivan’s Island
note_en: This is the island where the treasure hunt in The Gold-Bug takes place. Poe knew it well: he was stationed at Fort Moultrie here in 1827 and 1828, enlisted under the name Edgar A. Perry. The island hasn't forgotten him. There's a Poe Avenue, a Goldbug Avenue, and a library named after him
note: 《金甲虫》的寻宝故事就发生在这座岛上。坡 1827 至 1828 年以“埃德加·A·佩里”的化名在岛上的穆尔特里堡当兵，后来把这片沙滩写进了小说。如今岛上有坡大道、金甲虫大道，图书馆也以他命名

name: Charleston
note_en: The narrator of The Gold-Bug lives in Charleston and takes the boat over to Sullivan's Island to visit his friend Legrand. The story's famous code-breaking scene brought cryptography to ordinary readers for the first time and inspired a long line of detective and treasure-hunt stories
note: 《金甲虫》的叙述者住在查尔斯顿，常从城里过海去沙利文岛看望勒格朗。小说里破译藏宝密码的那一段让密码学第一次走进大众阅读，影响了后来许多侦探和寻宝故事

name: Wilmington
prototype_of: 《传统的精髓》里威灵顿的原型：切斯纳特把 1898 年的威明顿暴乱写进了这部小说——白人至上主义者以暴力推翻了民选的黑白联合市政府，常被称为美国本土唯一一次成功的政变。这是最早正面写这场暴行的小说之一
prototype_of_en: Wellington, the town in The Marrow of Tradition, stands in for Wilmington. Chesnutt based the novel on the 1898 Wilmington massacre, when armed white supremacists drove out the city's elected, racially mixed government. It's often called the only successful coup in American history, and his novel was one of the first to tell the story

name: Clyde
prototype_of: 《小城畸人》温斯堡的原型：舍伍德·安德森在克莱德度过童年和少年时代，书里那些孤独古怪的小镇人物，很多能在这里找到影子。镇上至今以“温斯堡”自豪
prototype_of_en: Clyde is the town behind Winesburg, Ohio. Sherwood Anderson grew up here, and many of the lonely, eccentric people in his stories were drawn from the neighbors he remembered. The town still proudly claims to be Winesburg

name: Franconia
note_en: Frost lived on a farm in the hills outside Franconia from 1915 to 1920. His long poem New Hampshire remembers watching election results flash up on the screen at the local movie theater. The farmhouse is now The Frost Place, a small museum that hosts a poet in residence every summer
note: 弗罗斯特 1915 至 1920 年在弗兰科尼亚山间的农场生活，长诗《新罕布什尔》里写到镇上电影院放映选举结果的一幕。他的农舍如今叫“弗罗斯特之家”，是博物馆，每年夏天还接待一位驻地诗人

name: Georgetown
note_en: In the early 1800s Patty Cannon ran a notorious gang on the Delmarva Peninsula that kidnapped free Black people and sold them into slavery in the South. She died in the Georgetown jail in 1829. George Alfred Townsend built his novel The Entailed Hat around her story
note: 帕蒂·坎农是 19 世纪初德尔马瓦半岛上臭名昭著的人贩子头目，专门绑架自由黑人卖往南方。1829 年她在乔治敦的监狱里死去。汤森的《世袭的帽子》以她为中心写了这段历史

name: Princess Anne
note_en: The Entailed Hat opens in this small Maryland county seat, with its courthouse, its churches, and its strict social order. Townsend grew up in Delaware and made his name as a Civil War correspondent, and in this novel he went back to the dark history of his own home peninsula
note: 《世袭的帽子》从这座马里兰小城开篇：法院、教堂和泾渭分明的社会等级。作者汤森是德拉瓦人、南北战争时的名记者，他写的正是自己家乡这片半岛的旧日阴影

name: Harriet Beecher Stowe House, Hartford
name_zh: 哈特福德 · 哈丽特·比彻·斯托故居
note_en: Uncle Tom's Cabin made Stowe one of the most famous writers in the world, and she spent her last twenty-plus years here in Hartford's Nook Farm neighborhood, right next door to Mark Twain. The house is now the Harriet Beecher Stowe Center, which tells the story of how her book changed the country
note: 《汤姆叔叔的小屋》让斯托成了世界上最有名的美国作家之一，晚年她在哈特福德的“书呆子农场”住了二十多年，隔壁就是马克·吐温的家。故居现为斯托中心，展出她的家具、手稿和这本书改变美国的故事

name: Harriet Beecher Stowe House, Brunswick
name_zh: 布伦斯威克 · 哈丽特·比彻·斯托故居
note_en: Stowe wrote Uncle Tom's Cabin in this house between 1850 and 1852. She later said the whole book started with a vision she had during a service at First Parish Church in town, where she suddenly saw Uncle Tom being beaten to death. She went home and wrote that scene first. The house belongs to Bowdoin College, and her writing room is open to visitors on certain days
note: 《汤姆叔叔的小屋》诞生的地方。1850 至 1852 年斯托住在这里，据她回忆，小说的念头来自镇上第一教区教堂的一次礼拜，她眼前浮现出汤姆被鞭打致死的情景，回家后先写下了这一章。房子现属鲍登学院，她的写作室按开放安排可以参观

name: Providence Athenaeum
name_zh: 普罗维登斯雅典娜图书馆
note_en: In 1848 Poe courted the poet Sarah Helen Whitman among the stacks of this library. According to a well-known story, when she asked him who wrote an unsigned poem in a magazine here, he signed his name under it on the spot. The poem was Ulalume. That December she broke off their engagement, also at the Athenaeum. The library is still open today
note: 1848 年坡在这座图书馆的书架间追求诗人莎拉·海伦·惠特曼。据说她曾问起一首匿名发表的诗，坡当场在杂志上签下自己的名字——那首诗就是《尤娜路姆》。同年 12 月，她也是在这里结束了两人的婚约。图书馆至今开放

name: Robert Frost Stone House Museum
name_zh: 沙夫茨伯里 · 罗伯特·弗罗斯特石屋博物馆
note_en: America's most famous winter poem was written in summer. On a hot June morning in 1922, Frost sat down at the dining table in this stone house and wrote Stopping by Woods on a Snowy Evening. It appeared in his collection New Hampshire, which won him the first of his four Pulitzer Prizes. He lived here from 1920 to 1929, and the house is now a museum
note: 美国最有名的雪夜诗写于盛夏：1922 年 6 月一个炎热的清晨，弗罗斯特在这座石屋的餐桌上写下了《雪夜林边小驻》，后来收进为他赢得第一个普利策奖的《新罕布什尔》。他 1920 至 1929 年住在这里，石屋现为博物馆
coord_checked: Robert Frost Stone House Museum — https://mapcarta.com/W1128346439

name: Hannibal
prototype_of: 汤姆·索亚和哈克的家乡圣彼得斯堡镇的原型：马克·吐温 1839 至 1853 年在汉尼拔长大，小说里的白篱笆、卡迪夫山、河边的木筏和洞穴都能在镇上找到。2024 年，珀西瓦尔·埃弗里特的《詹姆斯》从逃奴吉姆的视角重写了这段顺河而下的故事
prototype_of_en: The model for St. Petersburg, Tom Sawyer's and Huck's home town: Mark Twain grew up in Hannibal from 1839 to 1853, and the whitewashed fence, Cardiff Hill, the river rafts and the cave of the novels can all be found here. In 2024 Percival Everett's James retold the voyage down the river from the side of Jim, the runaway slave

name: Memphis
note_en: In 1858 the steamboat Pennsylvania exploded on the Mississippi. Twain's younger brother Henry, who had taken a job on the boat at Twain's urging, was badly burned and died a few days later in a makeshift hospital in Memphis. Twain later claimed he'd dreamed of Henry lying in a metal coffin before the accident. He never got over the loss, and he wrote about it in Life on the Mississippi
note: 1858 年宾夕法尼亚号汽船锅炉爆炸，吐温的弟弟亨利重伤，在孟菲斯的临时医院里去世，是吐温介绍他上船的。吐温后来说自己出事前梦见过弟弟躺在金属棺材里。《密西西比河上的生活》写下了这段他一生难忘的伤痛

name: Dubuque
note_en: In 1882 Twain went back to the Mississippi and took a steamboat all the way upriver. Once he gets above Dubuque, Life on the Mississippi stops worrying about snags and sandbars like an old riverboat pilot and starts describing the bluffs, the islands, and the color of the water. He thought this was the most beautiful stretch of the whole river
note: 1882 年吐温重回密西西比河，一路坐汽船北上。《密西西比河上的生活》写迪比克上游时，他放下了河道领航员的眼光，写起了峭壁、岛屿和水色——在他笔下，这是整条河最美的一段

name: Saint Paul
note_en: Saint Paul is where Twain's 1882 trip in Life on the Mississippi comes to an end. He had traveled all the way up from New Orleans, and here he found a young northern city that was growing fast
note: 《密西西比河上的生活》那趟 1882 年重返大河之旅的终点。吐温从新奥尔良一路北上，到圣保罗下了船，他在书里看到的是一座迅速长大的北方新城

name: New Orleans
note_en: When Twain was a riverboat pilot, New Orleans was the end of the line. Coming back in 1882, he wrote in Life on the Mississippi about levees that rose higher than the rooftops, the crowds on Canal Street, and Mardi Gras parades lit by torches
note: 当年吐温在这条河上做领航员，新奥尔良是航线的终点。1882 年重回旧地，他在《密西西比河上的生活》里写高过屋顶的河堤、运河街的人潮和火把照亮的狂欢节游行

name: Louisville
note_en: In Uncle Tom's Cabin, only the Ohio River separates Kentucky from the free states to the north. After Tom is sold down the river, his wife, Aunt Chloe, takes a job at a bakery in Louisville and saves every penny she can to buy him back
note: 《汤姆叔叔的小屋》里的肯塔基与自由州只隔一条俄亥俄河。汤姆被卖往南方后，克洛伊大娘到路易斯维尔给糕点铺做工，一分一分攒钱想把他赎回来

name: Chicago
note_en: Sister Carrie opens with eighteen-year-old Carrie on a train to Chicago, dazzled by the booming city's lights and shop windows. When the novel came out in 1900, it was considered so immoral that its own publisher barely sold it. Today it's seen as the book that launched American naturalism
note: 《嘉莉妹妹》开篇，十八岁的嘉莉坐火车来到正在疯长的芝加哥，被城市的灯火和橱窗吸引，一步步卷入欲望之中。这部书 1900 年出版时被认为有伤风化，出版社几乎没有发行，后来却被视为美国自然主义小说的开端

name: Indianapolis
prototype_of: 《伟大的安伯森家族》里那座中西部城市的原型：塔金顿生在印第安纳波利斯，看着它从马车小城变成工业城市。小说写一个旧家族随着汽车时代到来而没落，1919 年获普利策奖，后来奥逊·威尔斯把它拍成了电影
prototype_of_en: The unnamed Midwestern city in The Magnificent Ambersons is Indianapolis. Booth Tarkington was born here and watched it grow from a quiet town of horses and buggies into a sprawling industrial city. His novel about a proud old family ruined by the age of the automobile won the 1919 Pulitzer Prize, and Orson Welles later turned it into a film

name: Pepin
note_en: Laura Ingalls Wilder was born in the Big Woods near Pepin in 1867, and Little House in the Big Woods is the story of her early childhood there. When the family goes into town, it's Pepin they're visiting. A replica of the log cabin stands a few miles north of town
note: 劳拉·英格尔斯·怀尔德 1867 年生在佩平附近的大森林里，《大森林里的小木屋》写的就是这里的童年。书中一家人赶车进城买东西，就是来佩平。镇北有照原样复建的小木屋

name: Monroeville
prototype_of_en: Monroeville is the real Maycomb. Harper Lee grew up here, and her next-door neighbor and best friend as a child was Truman Capote, who became the model for Dill. The old courthouse on the town square is now a museum. Its courtroom was so iconic that Hollywood built an exact copy of it for the movie
prototype_of: 《杀死一只知更鸟》梅科姆镇的原型：哈珀·李在这里长大，童年的邻居和玩伴就是杜鲁门·卡波特，书里的迪儿正是以他为原型。镇中心的老法院如今是博物馆，电影里的法庭就是照它的样子搭的

name: Eatonton
prototype_of_en: The rural Georgia of The Color Purple comes from here. Alice Walker was born to a sharecropping family near Eatonton in 1944, and the voices, fields, and churches of the novel all come from this corner of the state. Eatonton is also the hometown of Joel Chandler Harris, who wrote the Uncle Remus stories
prototype_of: 《紫色》里西莉生活的佐治亚乡村：艾丽斯·沃克 1944 年生在伊顿顿附近的佃农家庭，小说的乡音、田地和教会都来自这里。镇上还出过另一位作家——《雷木斯大叔》的作者乔尔·钱德勒·哈里斯

name: Oxford
prototype_of_en: The model for Faulkner's town of Jefferson: he lived in Oxford almost all his life and built his imaginary Yoknapatawpha County out of the town and the county around it. The Compsons of The Sound and the Fury, the Bundrens hauling a coffin to town in As I Lay Dying, and Lena Grove and Joe Christmas of Light in August all live in this county. His home, Rowan Oak, is open to visitors, with the outline of a novel still written in his hand on the study wall
prototype_of: 福克纳笔下杰斐逊镇的原型：他一生几乎都住在牛津，用这座小城和周围的县造出了虚构的约克纳帕塔法县，《喧哗与骚动》的康普生家、《我弥留之际》里拉着棺材进城的本德伦一家、《八月之光》里的莉娜和乔·克里斯默斯都在这个县里。他的故居山楸橡树园对外开放，书房墙上还留着他亲手写的小说提纲

name: Eatonville
note_en: Founded in 1887, Eatonville was one of the first all-Black towns in America to govern itself. Zora Neale Hurston grew up here, and it's the town where Janie and Joe Starks run their store in Their Eyes Were Watching God. Joe is based on Eatonville's real mayor, Joe Clarke. The town celebrates its most famous daughter with a Zora festival every year
note: 1887 年建镇，是美国最早由黑人自治的城镇之一。赫斯顿在这里长大，《他们眼望上苍》里珍妮和乔·斯塔克斯开店的小镇就是伊顿维尔，乔的原型是真实的镇长乔·克拉克。镇上每年举办佐拉文化节

name: Jacksonville
note_en: Jacksonville marks a turning point in Their Eyes Were Watching God. After her husband Joe dies, Janie leaves Eatonville with the much younger Tea Cake, marries him here, and finally starts a life she has chosen for herself
note: 《他们眼望上苍》的转折点：珍妮在乔死后离开伊顿维尔，跟年轻的茶点来到杰克逊维尔结婚，开始她自己选择的生活。小说把这座海滨城市写成她第一次真正出走的地方

name: Seney
note_en: Big Two-Hearted River opens with Nick stepping off a train into a town that has burned to the ground. Seney had once been a booming lumber town. Hemingway came up here to fish in 1919, just back from the war, and turned that trip into one of his best-known stories
note: 《大双心河》开头，尼克下火车，看到的是一座被大火烧光的小镇。塞尼原是伐木热潮里的边疆镇。1919 年海明威从一战战场回来后来这里钓鱼，后来把这次旅行写成了他最有名的短篇之一

name: Fox River, Michigan
prototype_of_en: This is the river Hemingway actually fished in 1919. He liked the sound of the Two Hearted, a different river farther north, so he borrowed that name for his story. That means the river in Big Two-Hearted River isn't the Two Hearted on the map. It's the Fox
prototype_of: 《大双心河》里那条河的原型：海明威 1919 年真正钓鱼的是塞尼附近的福克斯河。他觉得北边另一条河“双心河”的名字更好听，就借了过来，所以小说里的河和地图上的双心河其实不是同一条

name: Fort Smith
note_en: In Lonesome Dove, Sheriff July Johnson leaves Fort Smith and heads across the plains to hunt down Jake Spoon. In the 1800s this border town was the gateway to Indian Territory and the home of Judge Isaac Parker's federal court. People called him the Hanging Judge
note: 《孤鸽镇》里阿肯色州的警长朱莱·约翰逊从史密斯堡出发，横穿大平原追捕凶手杰克·斯普恩。这座边境小城在十九世纪是通往印第安领地的门户，以“绞刑法官”帕克的联邦法院闻名

name: San Antonio
note_en: Two very different books meet in San Antonio. At the end of Lonesome Dove, Call keeps his promise to his old friend Gus and hauls his body three thousand miles from Montana back to Texas, to bury him in a grove near town where Gus once picnicked with the woman he loved. In O. Henry's A Fog in Santone, a sick young man wanders out into the fog that has settled over the city. O. Henry lived in San Antonio for a while too
note: 两本书在这里相遇。《孤鸽镇》结尾，考尔遵守承诺，把格斯的遗体从蒙大拿运回三千英里外的得克萨斯，葬在城外他们当年野餐的果园；欧·亨利的短篇《圣安东尼奥的雾》则让一个病人走进笼罩全城的雾。欧·亨利也在这座城里住过

name: Salt Lake City
note_en: In 1861 a young Samuel Clemens crossed the country by stagecoach with his older brother. They stopped in Salt Lake City for two days, and he even met the Mormon leader Brigham Young. In Roughing It he describes the city, ringed by mountains, with his usual dry humor
note: 1861 年年轻的塞缪尔·克莱门斯随哥哥坐驿车横穿大陆，在盐湖城停了两天，还见到了摩门教领袖杨百翰。《苦行记》里他用一贯的幽默写了这座群山环抱的城

name: Virginia City, Nevada
note_en: This is where Mark Twain was born, at least on paper. In February 1863 Samuel Clemens signed the name 'Mark Twain' for the first time, in the local newspaper, the Territorial Enterprise. In Roughing It he jokes about his days as a young reporter here, when he could turn a single hay wagon into several news stories
note: “马克·吐温”诞生的地方：1863 年 2 月，塞缪尔·克莱门斯在本地《领土企业报》上第一次用这个笔名署名。《苦行记》里，他还讲了自己当记者时怎么把一辆运草车编成好几条新闻

name: Honolulu
note_en: In 1866 the Sacramento Union sent Twain to Hawaii for four months. When he got back, his lectures about the islands made him a star on the stage. The later chapters of Roughing It tell the story of that trip, including all the fruit he ate
note: 1866 年吐温作为《萨克拉门托联合报》的通讯员在夏威夷待了四个月，回去后靠讲夏威夷见闻成了走红的演讲家。《苦行记》后半部分写的就是这趟旅行，包括这里的水果

name: Mount Hood
note_en: Standing on a bridge over the Willamette River in Portland, Muir watched the setting sun light up Mount Hood. The founder of the Sierra Club spent his life writing about the mountains of the West, and Steep Trails collects his travels in the Pacific Northwest
note: 缪尔站在波特兰的威拉米特河桥上，看夕阳把胡德山染成一片光。这位塞拉俱乐部的创始人一生为西部的山写作，《险峻的山径》收了他在太平洋西北的游记

name: Seattle
note_en: On his way to Alaska, Muir passed through Puget Sound when Seattle was still a small, new town competing with Tacoma to become the end of the railroad line. Travels in Alaska gives us a quick look at the city in its early days
note: 缪尔北上阿拉斯加时途经普吉特湾，那时的西雅图还是和塔科马争当铁路终点的新兴小镇。《阿拉斯加游记》留下了这座城市早年的一瞥

name: Tacoma, Washington
note_en: When Muir came through, Tacoma had just won the race to be the Northern Pacific Railroad's western terminus, and it was busy showing up its rival Seattle; Travels in Alaska catches the two young towns sizing each other up. In 1888 Muir climbed Mount Rainier, which you can see from here. On a clear day the mountain still looms over the city from the waterfront
note: 缪尔经过时，塔科马刚被选为北太平洋铁路的终点，正和西雅图较劲，《阿拉斯加游记》写下了两座新城互不服气的样子。缪尔 1888 年还登上了从这里就能望见的雷尼尔山。今天天气好时，站在港口边仍能看到雪山压在城市上方

name: Wrangell, Alaska
note_en: In 1879 Muir set out from Wrangell by canoe with the missionary S. Hall Young and a crew of Tlingit guides. They paddled into Glacier Bay, which hardly any outsiders had seen at the time. Muir's account in Travels in Alaska made the bay famous, and today it's a national park
note: 1879 年缪尔以兰格尔为基地，和传教士扬及特林吉特向导划独木舟北上，闯进了当时外人几乎不知道的冰川湾。《阿拉斯加游记》里的这段航行让冰川湾闻名，如今那里是国家公园

name: Medicine Bow, Wyoming
note_en: The Virginian, often called the first true Western novel, opens at this little railroad stop in Wyoming. It's here that the hero delivers the book's most famous line: 'When you call me that, smile!' The Virginian Hotel, built in 1911 and named after the novel, is still open for business
note: 第一部西部小说《弗吉尼亚人》从这个怀俄明铁路小站开场，那句名言“你这么叫我的时候，要笑着说”就发生在这里。镇上 1911 年盖的弗吉尼亚人旅馆以小说命名，至今营业

name: Ordway, South Dakota
note_en: Hamlin Garland's parents homesteaded near Ordway, in what was then Dakota Territory. In the preface to Main-Travelled Roads he describes coming back years later and seeing just how hard farm life was. That trip shaped the book, now a classic of Midwestern fiction
note: 加兰的父母在达科他领地开荒，就住在奥德韦附近。《大路》序言里，他回忆多年后重回这里，看到农民生活的艰辛，这本书因此成了写美国中西部农民的名作

name: Flagstaff, Arizona
note_en: Chapter 12 of The Grapes of Wrath follows Route 66 town by town, and Flagstaff is one of the stops. That same chapter is where Steinbeck called Route 66 'the mother road,' a nickname that has stuck ever since
note: 《愤怒的葡萄》第十二章写 66 号公路，一口气念出沿途城镇的名字，弗拉格斯塔夫是其中之一。斯坦贝克在这一章里把 66 号公路叫作“母亲之路”，这个名字从此跟着这条路

name: Sallisaw, Oklahoma
note_en: Sallisaw is the Joad family's home. The Grapes of Wrath opens with Tom, just out of prison, coming back to find that the bank has taken the farm and tractors have knocked down the house. Sallisaw wasn't actually in the worst part of the Dust Bowl, but thanks to the novel, it became the symbol of the Okie migration
note: 乔德一家的老家。《愤怒的葡萄》开篇，汤姆出狱回到萨利索附近，发现家里的农场已被银行收走、拖拉机推平。萨利索其实不在沙尘暴最严重的地带，但小说让它成了沙尘暴难民的代名词

name: Weedpatch Camp
prototype_of: 《愤怒的葡萄》里政府移民营地的原型：1936 年开放的阿尔文联邦营地，乔德一家在这里第一次得到尊严。斯坦贝克多次来访，营地主任汤姆·柯林斯就是书前献词里那位“亲身经历过的汤姆”。几座当年的营地建筑保留至今，加州正在考虑把这里建成州立公园
prototype_of_en: The government camp in The Grapes of Wrath, where the Joads are finally treated with dignity, was based on this one, the Arvin Federal Government Camp, which opened in 1936. Steinbeck visited often, and the camp's manager, Tom Collins, is the 'Tom who lived it' in the book's dedication. A few of the original buildings are still standing, and California is now considering turning the site into a state park

name: Denver
note_en: Denver is where Sal heads on his first trip west in On the Road, and it's Dean Moriarty's hometown. Dean was based on Neal Cassady, who grew up here. In 1947 Kerouac came to Denver to find him, and that trip became the backbone of the Beat Generation's defining novel
note: 《在路上》里萨尔第一次西行的目的地，是迪安·莫里亚蒂的家乡。迪安的原型尼尔·卡萨迪就在丹佛长大，1947 年凯鲁亚克来这里找他，后来写成了“垮掉的一代”的代表作

name: San Francisco
note_en: Two novels pass through San Francisco. The Sea-Wolf opens with a ferry sinking in thick fog on the bay, and the narrator is pulled from the water by Wolf Larsen's ship. In On the Road, Sal crosses the entire continent to get here and looks out at the Pacific before heading back
note: 两部小说在这里交会：《海狼》开篇，渡轮在旧金山湾的大雾里被撞沉，主人公落水后被“海狼”拉森的船救起；《在路上》里，萨尔一路横穿大陆，来到这座城市，又在离开前回望太平洋

name: Fargo, North Dakota
note_en: In 1960 Steinbeck set off across America in a camper truck with his poodle Charley. Ever since he was a boy, Fargo had seemed to him like the most far-off, mysterious name on the map, and in Travels with Charley he describes what it felt like to finally get there
note: 1960 年斯坦贝克带着狗查理开着露营车环游美国。他从小就觉得法戈是地图上最遥远、最神秘的地方，《与查理同行》写了他终于来到法戈时的感受

name: Billings, Montana
note_en: In Travels with Charley, Steinbeck declares 'I am in love with Montana' as soon as he crosses the state line, stops in Billings to buy himself a hat, and finds the people unhurried and kind. It's one of the warmest passages in the book. Billings is Montana's biggest city now, and trails along the Rimrocks, the sandstone cliffs north of town, look out over the city and the Yellowstone valley
note: 《与查理同行》里，斯坦贝克一进蒙大拿就说“我爱上了蒙大拿”，在比灵斯停下来买了一顶帽子，觉得这里的人从容又友善。这是全书最温暖的一段。比灵斯今天是蒙大拿最大的城市，城北那道砂岩悬崖“里姆罗克斯”上有步道，可以俯瞰全城和黄石河谷

name: Kuna, Idaho
note_en: In Angle of Repose, Susan Ward comes out to Idaho to join her husband and gets off the train at Kuna, a lonely station surrounded by sagebrush. Wallace Stegner based the novel on the letters of the writer and illustrator Mary Hallock Foote, and it won the Pulitzer Prize in 1972
note: 《安息角》里，苏珊·沃德来爱达荷与丈夫团聚，在库纳这个荒野小站下了火车。斯泰格纳以 19 世纪女作家兼插画家玛丽·哈洛克·富特的书信为底本写成这部小说，1972 年获普利策奖

name: Leadville, Colorado
note_en: Leadville was a mountain mining town at the height of Colorado's silver rush. The Wards in Angle of Repose live here for a while, just as Mary Hallock Foote and her husband did in 1879, the year the boom was at its wildest
note: 科罗拉多银矿热潮中的高山矿镇。《安息角》里沃德夫妇在这里度过一段时光，原型富特夫妇 1879 年确实住在莱德维尔，那是这座城最疯狂的年代

name: Boston
note_en: The Scarlet Letter opens with Hester, her baby in her arms and a scarlet A on her breast, on the scaffold of colonial Boston; Elizabeth Pain's gravestone in King's Chapel Burying Ground is said to have inspired her. More than two centuries later, Henry James's The Bostonians sets Olive Chancellor, a Boston feminist, against her Southern cousin in a struggle for the young speaker Verena Tarrant
note: 《红字》开篇，海丝特抱着婴儿、胸前戴着红色的 A 字，站在殖民地波士顿的刑台上示众，国王礼拜堂墓地里伊丽莎白·佩恩的墓碑相传就是她的原型。两百多年后，亨利·詹姆斯的《波士顿人》写这座城里的女权运动者奥利芙，和她的南方表亲争夺年轻的女演说家维丽娜

name: Salem Custom House
note_en: This is where The Scarlet Letter began. Hawthorne worked here as the surveyor from 1846 to 1849, and after he lost the job, he wrote the novel. In the book's introduction he claims he found a faded scarlet A and an old manuscript in a room upstairs, which is of course part of the fiction. The Custom House is now part of a national historic site, and you can see his office
note: 《红字》是从这里来的：霍桑 1846 至 1849 年在海关当检查官，丢了这份差事后写成了小说。他在序言里说，自己在楼上一间旧屋里找到一块褪色的红布 A 字和一份旧手稿——这当然是小说家的设计。海关大楼现属国家公园，可以看到他的办公室

name: Emily Dickinson Museum, Homestead
name_zh: 阿默斯特 · 艾米莉·狄金森故居博物馆
note_en: Emily Dickinson was born in this house in 1830 and barely left Amherst her whole life. In her later years she hardly left the house at all. After she died, her sister found nearly 1,800 poems tucked away in her bedroom. Only about ten had ever been published. The Homestead and her brother's house next door, the Evergreens, now make up the Emily Dickinson Museum, and you can visit the room where she wrote
note: 狄金森 1830 年生在这座宅邸，一生几乎没有离开阿默斯特，后半生更是很少走出家门。她去世后，妹妹在她卧室里发现了近一千八百首诗，其中只有十来首在生前发表过。故居和隔壁哥哥的常青居组成博物馆，可以看到她写诗的卧室

name: The Mount
name_zh: 莱诺克斯 · 蒙特庄园
note_en: Edith Wharton designed this house herself, following the ideas she'd laid out in her book The Decoration of Houses. She lived here from 1902 to 1911 and wrote her first bestseller, The House of Mirth, at The Mount. The old New York high society she later wrote about in The Age of Innocence was the world she grew up in
note: 华顿亲自设计的宅邸，把她和建筑师合写的《房屋装饰》里的主张全盖了出来。她 1902 至 1911 年住在这里，写成了第一部畅销小说《欢乐之家》。后来的《纯真年代》写的老纽约上流社会，正是她在这里过的那种生活

name: Hartford
note_en: Hartford gave Dickens a huge welcome on his first trip to America in 1842. In American Notes he describes the town and the Charter Oak, the tree where colonists supposedly hid Connecticut's charter (it came down in a storm in 1856). He also writes about the conversations he had with patients at the local asylum
note: 1842 年狄更斯首次访美，在哈特福德受到盛大欢迎。《美国札记》写了这座小城和传说中藏过殖民地特许状的宪章橡树（这棵树 1856 年倒下），还记下了他在精神病院里和病人的交谈

name: New Haven
note_en: Passing through New Haven in 1842, Dickens admired Yale's buildings set among long rows of elm trees and felt that town and country had somehow met here. New Haven was already known as the Elm City, though most of those old elms were later killed by Dutch elm disease
note: 1842 年狄更斯路过纽黑文，看到耶鲁的校舍掩映在一排排榆树下，说这里仿佛是城市和乡村握了手。纽黑文本来就以“榆树之城”著称，可惜那些老榆树后来大多死于荷兰榆树病

name: Site of the Academy of Music
name_zh: 纽约音乐学院歌剧院旧址
note_en: The Age of Innocence begins here: 'On a January evening of the early seventies, Christine Nilsson was singing in Faust at the Academy of Music in New York.' This opera house was the stronghold of old New York society. The newly rich couldn't get boxes, so in 1883 they built their own opera house, the Metropolitan. The Academy was torn down in 1926. It stood at 14th Street and Irving Place
note: 《纯真年代》开篇第一句：七十年代初一个一月的晚上，克丽丝汀·尼尔松正在音乐学院唱《浮士德》。这座歌剧院是老纽约世家的地盘，新富们挤不进包厢，就在 1883 年另建了大都会歌剧院。原楼 1926 年拆除，原址在十四街和欧文广场路口
coord_checked: Site of the Academy of Music — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_of_Music_(New_York_City)

name: Lower Fifth Avenue at Washington Square
name_zh: 华盛顿广场旁的第五大道南端
note_en: Washington Square and lower Fifth Avenue were home to the old-money families of The Age of Innocence. Walking up the avenue, Newland Archer moves through a world where keeping up appearances matters more than anything. Wharton herself was born just a few blocks away, on West 23rd Street
note: 华盛顿广场和第五大道南端是《纯真年代》里老纽约世家住的地方。纽兰·阿切尔沿着这条大道向北走，一路走过他那个讲究体面、不容越界的世界。华顿本人也出生在离这里不远的西二十三街
coord_checked: Lower Fifth Avenue at Washington Square — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Square_Arch

name: Wheeling
prototype_of: 《铁厂的生活》里那座炼铁城镇的原型：丽贝卡·哈丁·戴维斯在惠灵长大，看着工人在高炉边耗尽一生。这篇小说 1861 年匿名发表在《大西洋月刊》上，被认为是美国现实主义文学的开端之一
prototype_of_en: The iron town in Life in the Iron Mills is Wheeling. Rebecca Harding Davis grew up here, watching workers wear out their lives in front of the furnaces. Her story appeared anonymously in The Atlantic in 1861, and it's now considered one of the first works of American realism

name: Edgar Allan Poe House and Museum
name_zh: 巴尔的摩 · 埃德加·爱伦·坡故居博物馆
note_en: From about 1833 to 1835, Poe lived in this tiny brick house with his aunt, Maria Clemm, and his young cousin Virginia, who would later become his wife. He wrote some of his early stories here, and one of them, MS. Found in a Bottle, won a prize from a Baltimore newspaper. It was the first real money he'd ever made from writing. Poe is buried in Baltimore too
note: 坡和姨母玛丽亚·克莱姆一家约 1833 至 1835 年挤在这座小砖房里，阁楼一样的小房间里住着后来成为他妻子的表妹弗吉尼亚。他在这里写出早期短篇，《瓶中手稿》赢得巴尔的摩一家报纸的征文奖，第一次拿到了稿费。坡最后也葬在巴尔的摩
coord_checked: Edgar Allan Poe House and Museum — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Allan_Poe_House_and_Museum

name: Edgar Allan Poe National Historic Site
name_zh: 费城 · 埃德加·爱伦·坡国家历史遗址
note_en: Poe lived at several addresses in Philadelphia, but this is the only one still standing. He was here in 1843 and 1844, during the most productive stretch of his career, when The Gold-Bug came out and became a hit. Visitors say the cellar looks a lot like the one in The Black Cat, where a body is walled up, and there's a raven statue out front. It's run by the National Park Service and free to visit
note: 坡在费城住过好几处，只有这一处留存下来。1843 至 1844 年他住在这里，正是创作最旺盛的时期，《金甲虫》就在这时发表并大获成功。故居地下室被认为很像《黑猫》里把尸体砌进墙里的那间，门前还立着一只乌鸦雕塑。现属国家公园管理局，免费开放
coord_checked: Edgar Allan Poe National Historic Site — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Allan_Poe_National_Historic_Site

name: Santa Clara Valley
note_en: The Call of the Wild opens on Judge Miller's sunny estate in California, where Buck lives like a king until he's stolen and shipped off to the Klondike. The estate was based on Judge Hiram Bond's ranch in the Santa Clara Valley. Jack London met Bond's sons and their big dog during the gold rush, and that dog became Buck
note: 《野性的呼唤》开篇，巴克是加州阳光下米勒法官庄园里的大狗，直到被偷走卖往克朗代克。法官庄园以圣克拉拉谷的邦德法官家为原型；杰克·伦敦在淘金地认识了邦德家的儿子和他们的狗，那只狗就是巴克的原型

name: Old General Land Office, Austin
name_zh: 奥斯汀 · 旧土地总署
note_en: O. Henry worked as a draftsman in this castle-like stone building from 1887 to 1891, and later used it as the setting for several stories, including Bexar Scrip No. 2692. Today it's the Texas Capitol Visitors Center
note: 欧·亨利 1887 至 1891 年在这座德国城堡式的石楼里当绘图员，后来把它写进了好几个短篇，《贝克萨土地凭证第 2692 号》就发生在这里。大楼现为得克萨斯州议会大厦游客中心

name: Red Cloud (Black Hawk prototype)
name_zh: 雷德克劳德（黑鹰镇原型）
prototype_of_en: Black Hawk, the town in My Ántonia, is based on Red Cloud. Willa Cather moved here from Virginia when she was nine and grew up on the Nebraska prairie. Red Cloud shows up under different names in six of her novels. The National Willa Cather Center offers tours of the opera house, train depot, and homes that appear in her books
prototype_of: 《我的安东妮亚》黑鹰镇的原型：凯瑟九岁随家人从弗吉尼亚搬到内布拉斯加，在雷德克劳德长大。她六部小说里的小镇都能在这里找到原型，镇上的国家薇拉·凯瑟中心可以参观她写进书里的歌剧院、火车站和房屋

name: Cathedral Basilica of Saint Francis of Assisi
name_zh: 圣菲 · 阿西西圣方济各主教座堂
prototype_of: 《死神来迎接大主教》里拉图尔主教那座教堂的原型：真实的拉米大主教 1869 年起在圣菲修建这座罗马式大教堂，凯瑟以他为原型写了小说。拉米的铜像立在教堂门前，他本人就葬在教堂里
prototype_of_en: This is the cathedral that Bishop Latour dreams of building in Death Comes for the Archbishop. Cather based Latour on the real Archbishop Jean-Baptiste Lamy, who began building this Romanesque cathedral in Santa Fe in 1869. His bronze statue stands by the entrance, and he's buried inside

name: Wolf House ruins
name_zh: 格伦埃伦 · 狼屋遗址
note_en: Jack London poured his book money into his dream house, built from volcanic stone and redwood. In August 1913, just days before he and his wife were going to move in, it burned down in a single night. The stone walls that survived are the ruins you see today. London died three years later, and his ashes are buried on a small hill nearby, under a big red boulder
note: 杰克·伦敦用版税盖的梦想之家，石头和红木建了两年，1913 年 8 月在完工前夕一夜烧毁，他和妻子一天也没住过。烧剩的石墙就是今天的废墟。他三年后去世，骨灰埋在废墟附近的小山丘上，压着一块红色熔岩巨石

name: Willa Cather Childhood Home
name_zh: 雷德克劳德 · 薇拉·凯瑟童年故居
note_en: As a teenager, Willa Cather lived in the attic of this house and put up the wallpaper herself. Much of that wallpaper is still there. She later gave her attic room to Thea, the heroine of The Song of the Lark. The house reopened for tours in 2023 after a restoration
note: 凯瑟十几岁时住在这座房子的阁楼里，墙纸是她自己贴上去的，这些墙纸大部分保存至今。后来她在《云雀之歌》里把这间阁楼写成了主人公西娅的小屋。故居修复后 2023 年重新开放导览

name: O. Henry Museum, Austin
name_zh: 奥斯汀 · 欧·亨利博物馆
note_en: O. Henry lived in this cottage from 1893 to 1895, back when he was still William Sydney Porter, and ran a humor weekly called The Rolling Stone. Not long after, he was charged with embezzling money from the bank where he'd worked. It was in prison that he started writing stories under the name O. Henry. The cottage is now a museum, and every year it hosts the O. Henry Pun-Off
note: 1893 至 1895 年，还叫威廉·西德尼·波特的欧·亨利在这里住，同时办了一份幽默周刊《滚石》。不久他被控挪用银行公款，后来在狱中开始用“欧·亨利”这个笔名写小说。小屋现为博物馆，每年还举办“欧·亨利双关语大赛”

name: Ingalls homesite near Independence
name_zh: 独立城附近 · 英格尔斯旧居遗址
prototype_of: 《草原上的小木屋》的原型：1869 至 1871 年英格尔斯一家在这里开荒，爸爸亲手盖起小木屋。原址上复建了小木屋，旁边保留着当年的学校和邮局
prototype_of_en: This is the real Little House on the Prairie. The Ingalls family homesteaded here from 1869 to 1871, and Pa built the cabin with his own hands. A replica cabin now stands on the site, along with an old one-room schoolhouse and post office

name: Atlanta
note_en: Atlanta is the city of Gone with the Wind. It's where Scarlett dances at the charity bazaar, nurses wounded soldiers, and finally flees as the city burns. Margaret Mitchell wrote the novel between 1926 and 1929 in a cramped Midtown apartment she nicknamed 'the Dump.' The building is now the Margaret Mitchell House museum
note: 《飘》的城市。斯嘉丽在战时的亚特兰大参加义卖舞会、照料伤兵，又在城市陷落的大火中逃出。玛格丽特·米切尔 1926 至 1929 年在市中心一间被她叫作“垃圾堆”的小公寓里写成了这部小说，公寓楼现为玛格丽特·米切尔故居博物馆

name: French Quarter, New Orleans
note_en: In 1882 Twain strolled through the French Quarter with the novelist George Washington Cable, taking in the weathered stucco walls and lacy iron balconies. Cable was famous at the time for his stories about Creole New Orleans, and Life on the Mississippi describes their walk together
note: 1882 年吐温和作家乔治·华盛顿·凯布尔一起漫步法国区，看风雨染色的灰泥墙和铁艺阳台。凯布尔写新奥尔良克里奥尔人的小说当时正红，《密西西比河上的生活》里写了这次同游

name: West End, New Orleans
note_en: West End was the lakeside resort where New Orleans went to relax on weekends. In Life on the Mississippi, Twain has dinner on a terrace overlooking Lake Pontchartrain, enjoying the evening breeze and the lights on the water
note: 当年新奥尔良人周末消遣的湖滨度假区。吐温在《密西西比河上的生活》里写自己坐在庞恰特雷恩湖上的露台吃饭，看着湖面的晚风和灯光

name: Mark Twain Cave
prototype_of: 《汤姆·索亚历险记》里麦克杜格尔洞的原型：汤姆和贝琪在洞里迷路三天，印第安·乔最后困死在洞口。吐温小时候常来这里探险。洞穴至今开放导览，路线里能看到书里写到的地方
prototype_of_en: This is McDougal's Cave from Tom Sawyer, where Tom and Becky get lost for three days and where Injun Joe dies trapped behind the sealed door. Twain explored this cave as a boy, and it's still open for guided tours that take you past spots from the book

name: St. Louis
note: 《哈克贝利·费恩历险记》里，哈克和吉姆夜里乘木筏顺流而下，从河上看圣路易斯的万家灯火铺满岸边，整座城一点声音也没有。这是全书写河夜最美的段落之一
note_en: In Huckleberry Finn, Huck and Jim drift past St. Louis on their raft in the middle of the night and see the city's lights stretched out along the shore, without a sound. It's one of the most beautiful night scenes on the river in the whole book

name: Mark Twain Boyhood Home
note: 汤姆·索亚的家：马克·吐温在这座白房子里度过少年时代，门前就是汤姆骗小伙伴替他刷的那道白篱笆。街对面是贝琪·撒切尔原型劳拉·霍金斯的家。故居和周边几座房子组成博物馆
note_en: This white house is where Mark Twain grew up, and where Tom Sawyer lives. Out front is the fence that Tom tricks his friends into whitewashing for him. Across the street is the house of Laura Hawkins, the girl who inspired Becky Thatcher. The house and the buildings around it make up the Mark Twain Boyhood Home and Museum

name: H. P. Lovecraft’s grave, Swan Point Cemetery
name_zh: 普罗维登斯 · 洛夫克拉夫特之墓（天鹅角公墓）
note_en: Lovecraft's headstone carries just three words, 'I Am Providence', a line from one of his letters with a neat double meaning: the city he could never leave, and fate itself. After two miserable years in New York he came home and wrote Providence into his cosmic horror. When he was buried in 1937 his name went only on the family monument; fans raised this stone for him in 1977
note: 墓碑上只有一句“I Am Providence”，出自洛夫克拉夫特的书信，一语双关：既是他一生离不开的普罗维登斯，又是“天意”。他在纽约潦倒两年后回到家乡，把这座城写进了自己的恐怖宇宙。他下葬时只在家族碑上有个名字，这块墓碑是书迷 1977 年为他立的

name: 135 Benefit Street (the Shunned House)
name_zh: 普罗维登斯 · 贝尼菲特街135号（“凶宅”）
note_en: Lovecraft's story The Shunned House is about this real house. It opens by pointing out that Edgar Allan Poe, while courting Sarah Helen Whitman in Providence, used to walk right past this door on Benefit Street, never guessing what was inside. It's a private home, so view it from the street
note: 洛夫克拉夫特小说《凶宅》写的就是这座真实的房子。小说开头说，当年坡在普罗维登斯追求惠特曼夫人时，常沿着贝尼菲特街散步，每次都从这座房子门前走过，却不知道它的秘密。现为私宅，只能在街上看

name: Buxton, Maine
note_en: This is the setting of the most moving promise in Shawshank. Andy tells Red that if he ever gets out, he should go to a hayfield in Buxton, follow a stone wall to a big oak tree, and look for a piece of black volcanic glass that has no business being in a Maine field. When Red is paroled, he goes. The hayfield is fictional, but the town is real
note: 《肖申克的救赎》里最动人的约定：安迪告诉瑞德，出狱后去巴克斯顿一片干草地，沿着石墙走到一棵橡树下，找一块不属于缅因州的黑色火山岩。瑞德假释后真的来了。干草地是虚构的，小镇是真的

name: Ohio State Reformatory, Mansfield
name_zh: 曼斯菲尔德 · 俄亥俄州立感化院
scene: 片中的肖申克监狱：典狱长办公室、假释听证室和安迪逃出去的地道都在这里拍摄。故事设在缅因州，电影却是在俄亥俄这座 1896 年的城堡式监狱里拍的；监狱 1990 年关闭，如今开放参观，还有“肖申克步道”串起周边取景地
scene_en: this is Shawshank prison. The warden's office, the parole board scenes, and Andy's escape route were all filmed here. The story takes place in Maine, but the movie was shot at this castle-like prison in Ohio, which opened in 1896 and closed in 1990. It's now open for tours, and the Shawshank Trail will take you to other filming locations nearby

name: Virginia Park, Ann Arbor
name_zh: 安娜堡 · 弗吉尼亚公园
scene: 朱莉爬上去不肯下来的那棵梧桐树：2009年夏天在这座公园拍摄。这里原本是两棵并排的悬铃木，后期用特效去掉了一棵，成了片中孤零零的一棵大树
scene_en: the sycamore tree Juli climbs and refuses to come down from was filmed in this park in the summer of 2009. There were actually two trees standing side by side here, and the filmmakers digitally removed one to create the movie's lone sycamore

name: Evangeline Oak, St. Martinville
name_zh: 圣马丁维尔 · 伊万杰琳橡树
note: 朗费罗的长诗《伊万杰琳》写阿卡迪亚人被英军逐出新斯科舍，伊万杰琳一路寻找失散的恋人，来到路易斯安那的泰什河畔。圣马丁维尔是阿卡迪亚流亡者在这里的落脚点，镇上把河边一棵老橡树叫作伊万杰琳橡树，相传她就在树下等过恋人
note_en: Longfellow's Evangeline follows an Acadian girl driven out of Nova Scotia by the British, searching for her lost lover all the way to the Bayou Teche in Louisiana. St. Martinville was where many Acadian exiles settled, and the town calls an old oak on the bayou the Evangeline Oak, where legend says she waited for him

name: The House of the Seven Gables, Salem
prototype_of: 霍桑《七角楼》里品钦家那座被诅咒的老宅的原型。房子建于 1668 年，霍桑的远房表姐住在这里，他常来做客，听她讲房子早年有七个尖顶。现在是博物馆，可以钻进壁炉旁那道窄小的暗梯，霍桑出生的老房子也被搬到了同一个院子里
prototype_of_en: The model for the cursed Pyncheon house in Hawthorne's novel. Built in 1668, it belonged to Hawthorne's cousin, whom he often visited and who told him the house had once had seven gables. It is now a museum where you can climb the narrow secret staircase beside the chimney, and the house where Hawthorne was born has been moved onto the same grounds
coord_checked: House of the Seven Gables (Wikimedia Commons) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Category:House_of_the_Seven_Gables

name: Wall Street, Manhattan
note: 梅尔维尔《抄写员巴特比》的副标题就是“一个华尔街的故事”。巴特比在华尔街一家律师事务所里抄文件，对着窗外一堵砖墙，什么都用一句“我宁愿不”回绝，最后死在监狱里。今天的华尔街高楼林立，那堵墙已经无处可寻，但窄街和老教堂还在
note_en: Melville's Bartleby is subtitled 'A Story of Wall Street.' Bartleby copies documents in a Wall Street law office facing a brick wall, answers every request with 'I would prefer not to,' and ends up dying in prison. Today the street is lined with towers and the wall is long gone, but the narrow street and Trinity Church at its head are still there

name: Fulton Ferry Landing, Brooklyn
name_zh: 布鲁克林 · 富尔顿渡口
note: 惠特曼在《草叶集》的《过布鲁克林渡口》里，站在曼哈顿和布鲁克林之间的渡船上，对着百年后的读者说话：你们看到的河水和海鸥，我也看过。那时还没有布鲁克林大桥，这里就是渡船靠岸的地方。现在是布鲁克林大桥公园的一角，栏杆上刻着这首诗的诗句
note_en: In 'Crossing Brooklyn Ferry,' from Leaves of Grass, Whitman stands on the ferry between Manhattan and Brooklyn and speaks to readers a hundred years later: the river and the gulls you see, I saw too. There was no Brooklyn Bridge yet, and this was where the ferry came in. It is now a corner of Brooklyn Bridge Park, with lines from the poem set into the railing
coord_checked: Fulton Ferry Landing (Brooklyn Bridge Park) (Wikimedia Commons) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Category:Fulton_Ferry_Landing_(Brooklyn_Bridge_Park)

name: Fell's Point, Baltimore
name_zh: 巴尔的摩 · 费尔斯角
note: 道格拉斯少年时被送到巴尔的摩，在这一带的主人家里偷偷学会识字，后来又在费尔斯角的造船厂干活，挨过白人工人的毒打。1838 年他扮成水手，从这里坐火车逃往北方。《道格拉斯自述》写了他在巴尔的摩的日子，为保护帮过他的人，逃跑的细节没写。码头区的砖房和石子路至今保存完好
note_en: As a boy Douglass was sent to Baltimore, where he secretly taught himself to read in his master's house; later he worked in the shipyards at Fell's Point and was savagely beaten by white workers. In 1838 he escaped north by train from this city, disguised as a sailor. The Narrative tells of his Baltimore years, leaving out how he escaped to protect those who helped him. The brick houses and cobbled streets of the waterfront are still well preserved

name: Frederick Douglass National Historic Site (Cedar Hill)
name_zh: 华盛顿 · 道格拉斯故居（雪松山）
note: 逃出奴隶制的道格拉斯晚年住在华盛顿东南的这座山坡宅院里，从 1877 年住到 1895 年去世。他在这里写完最后一部自传，后院有他读书写作的石头小屋，他叫它“咆哮室”。故居由国家公园管理局开放，屋里大部分家具和藏书都是原物
note_en: Douglass, who had escaped slavery, spent his last years in this hilltop house in southeast Washington, from 1877 until his death in 1895. He finished his last autobiography here, and behind the house is the little stone cabin where he read and wrote, which he called 'the Growlery.' The National Park Service runs it, and most of the furniture and books are his own
coord_checked: Frederick Douglass National Historic Site (Wikimedia Commons) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Category:Frederick_Douglass_National_Historic_Site

name: Washington Square Park, Manhattan
name_zh: 曼哈顿 · 华盛顿广场
note: 詹姆斯《华盛顿广场》里的斯洛珀医生和女儿凯瑟琳就住在广场北边的红砖排屋里，詹姆斯自己的祖母也住在这一排。一百年后，鲍德温《另一个国家》里的人物在广场周围的格林威治村喝酒、相爱、绝望。凯旋门和广场北侧那排老房子都还在
note_en: In James's Washington Square, Dr. Sloper and his daughter Catherine live in the red-brick row on the north side of the square, where James's own grandmother lived. A century later the characters of Baldwin's Another Country drink, love and despair in the Greenwich Village streets around it. The arch and the old row on the north side are still there

name: Grand Isle, Louisiana
name_zh: 路易斯安那 · 格兰德岛
note: 肖邦《觉醒》开篇，新奥尔良的有钱人家在这座墨西哥湾的小岛上避暑，艾德娜在这里第一次学会游泳，也第一次意识到自己想要另一种生活。小说结尾她又回到这片海里。岛上现在是钓鱼和观鸟的去处，州立公园有长长的海滩
note_en: The Awakening opens on this Gulf of Mexico island, where wealthy New Orleans families spend the summer; here Edna learns to swim and first realises she wants another kind of life, and at the end of the novel she returns to this sea. Today the island is known for fishing and birdwatching, and the state park has a long beach

name: Chancellorsville Battlefield, Virginia
name_zh: 弗吉尼亚 · 钱斯勒斯维尔战场
prototype_of: 克莱恩《红色英勇勋章》里那场没有名字的战役，一般认为写的就是 1863 年的钱斯勒斯维尔战役。克莱恩生于战后，没打过仗，全凭老兵的回忆写出了一个新兵临阵脱逃又回到队伍的心理。战场现在属于弗雷德里克斯堡和斯波特瑟尔韦尼亚国家军事公园，有步道和讲解牌
prototype_of_en: The unnamed battle in The Red Badge of Courage is generally taken to be Chancellorsville, fought in 1863. Crane was born after the war and never saw combat, yet from veterans' memories he wrote the inner life of a recruit who runs from battle and then returns to his regiment. The battlefield is now part of a national military park, with trails and markers

name: Fort William Henry, Lake George
name_zh: 乔治湖 · 威廉·亨利堡
note: 库珀《最后的莫希干人》写的就是 1757 年威廉·亨利堡之围：英军向法军投降后撤出要塞，途中遭到法军的印第安盟军袭击。小说里门罗上校的两个女儿正是要赶到这座堡里去。现在的木堡是按原样重建的，做成了博物馆，就在乔治湖南岸
note_en: The Last of the Mohicans is built around the siege of Fort William Henry in 1757, when the British surrendered to the French and were attacked by France's Native allies as they marched out. Colonel Munro's two daughters are trying to reach this fort when the novel opens. The log fort, rebuilt as it was, is now a museum on the south shore of Lake George

name: Big Moose Lake, Adirondacks
name_zh: 阿迪朗达克 · 大穆斯湖
prototype_of: 德莱塞《美国的悲剧》取材于真实案件：1906 年切斯特·吉莱特带着怀孕的女友格雷丝·布朗来到阿迪朗达克山区的大穆斯湖划船，她溺死在湖里，他后来被判死刑。小说里的“大苦水湖”就是这里。湖边至今还是安静的度假屋和划船码头
prototype_of_en: An American Tragedy is drawn from a real case: in 1906 Chester Gillette took his pregnant girlfriend Grace Brown out in a rowboat on Big Moose Lake in the Adirondacks, she drowned, and he was later executed. The novel's Big Bittern Lake is this lake. Its shores are still quiet cabins and boat docks
coord_checked: File:Big Moose Lake - Gazebo Dock.jpg (geotagged, Wikimedia Commons) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Big_Moose_Lake_-_Gazebo_Dock.jpg

name: Jack London Square, Oakland
name_zh: 奥克兰 · 杰克·伦敦广场
note: 杰克·伦敦在奥克兰长大，少年时在这片码头当过蚝贼，在海诺尔德的“第一家也是最后一家机会”酒馆里读书、听水手讲故事。《马丁·伊登》里那个靠自学当上作家的奥克兰水手，很大程度上就是他自己。那家 1883 年开的小酒馆还在营业，地板歪得厉害
note_en: Jack London grew up in Oakland, raided oyster beds off this waterfront as a teenager, and read and listened to sailors' stories in Heinold's First and Last Chance Saloon. Martin Eden, the self-taught Oakland sailor who becomes a writer, is largely London himself. The little saloon, open since 1883, still serves drinks on its badly tilted floor
coord_checked: Jack London Square, Oakland, California (Wikimedia Commons) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Category:Jack_London_Square,_Oakland,_California

name: Pete's Tavern, Irving Place
note: 欧·亨利 1903 至 1907 年住在对面的欧文广场 55 号，这家号称纽约最老的酒馆说他就是在店里第二个卡座写出了《麦琪的礼物》，不过这多半是传说。故事里那对用头发和金表换礼物的穷夫妻，就是他笔下“四百万”纽约小人物中的一对。酒馆至今营业
note_en: O. Henry lived across the street at 55 Irving Place from 1903 to 1907, and this tavern, which calls itself the oldest in New York, says he wrote The Gift of the Magi in its second booth, though that is probably legend. The poor young couple who trade hair and watch for Christmas gifts are two of his 'four million' ordinary New Yorkers. The tavern is still open

name: Tuolumne Meadows, Yosemite
name_zh: 约塞米蒂 · 图奥勒米草甸
note: 1869 年，三十一岁的缪尔跟着一群羊上山放牧，在约塞米蒂高地过了一个夏天，《夏日走过山间》就是那年的日记，最后几周写的正是图奥勒米草甸。他后来力主在这里设立国家公园。现在草甸是高山徒步的起点，夏天才能开车上来
note_en: In 1869 the thirty-one-year-old Muir went up into the Yosemite high country with a flock of sheep and spent the summer there; My First Summer in the Sierra is his journal of that year, and its last weeks are spent in Tuolumne Meadows. He later campaigned for the national park. The meadows are now a starting point for high-country hikes, reachable by road only in summer

name: Robert Frost Farm, Derry
name_zh: 德里 · 罗伯特·弗罗斯特农场
note: 弗罗斯特 1900 至 1911 年在这座新罕布什尔的农场种地养鸡，日子过得很穷，却积下了后来《波士顿以北》里的大部分题材：修墙的邻居、雇工之死、乡下人的家长里短。他说这些年是他一生的根。农舍和谷仓保存下来，屋后有一条走得到那段石墙的小路
note_en: Frost farmed and kept chickens on this New Hampshire farm from 1900 to 1911, poor but gathering most of the material for North of Boston: the neighbour mending wall, the death of the hired man, the talk of country people. He called these years the core of his life. The farmhouse and barn survive, and a path behind the house leads to the stone wall
coord_checked: Robert Frost Farm State Historic Site (Wikimedia Commons) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Category:Robert_Frost_Farm_State_Historic_Site

name: Ernest Hemingway House, Key West
name_zh: 基韦斯特 · 海明威故居
note: 海明威 1931 至 1939 年住在基韦斯特的这座西班牙殖民风格的房子里，常从这里出海去古巴附近的湾流钓大马林鱼，后来写成了《老人与海》里老渔夫和大鱼搏斗的故事（小说发生在古巴）。故居现为博物馆，院子里住着几十只六趾猫，据说是他那只猫的后代
note_en: Hemingway lived in this Spanish Colonial house in Key West from 1931 to 1939, and from here he went out into the Gulf Stream toward Cuba after marlin, the experience behind the old fisherman's fight in The Old Man and the Sea (which is set in Cuba). The house is a museum, and dozens of six-toed cats, said to descend from his, live in the garden

name: Steinbeck House, Salinas
name_zh: 萨利纳斯 · 斯坦贝克故居
note: 斯坦贝克 1902 年生在这座维多利亚式小楼里，在萨利纳斯长大。《伊甸之东》写萨利纳斯谷两个家族几代人的恩怨，书里的汉密尔顿家就是他外祖父一家，他自己也以叙述者身份出现。故居现在是一家午餐餐厅，镇上还有国家斯坦贝克中心
note_en: Steinbeck was born in this Victorian house in 1902 and grew up in Salinas. East of Eden follows two families through generations in the Salinas Valley; the Hamiltons are his mother's family, and he appears himself as the narrator. The house is now a lunch restaurant, and the National Steinbeck Center is nearby in town

name: Walnut Grove and Plum Creek, Minnesota
name_zh: 明尼苏达 · 沃尔纳特格罗夫（梅溪）
note: 《梅溪岸边》里，英格尔斯一家搬到明尼苏达，先住在梅溪岸边挖进土坡的地洞屋里，后来盖了木屋，又遇上蝗灾。镇外的梅溪边还能看到那个地洞屋留下的凹坑，镇上有劳拉·英格尔斯·怀尔德博物馆，每年夏天演出露天剧
note_en: In On the Banks of Plum Creek the Ingalls family moves to Minnesota, lives first in a dugout cut into the creek bank, then builds a frame house and is hit by a plague of grasshoppers. Outside town you can still see the hollow left by the dugout beside the creek, and Walnut Grove has a Laura Ingalls Wilder Museum and an outdoor pageant every summer

name: Peterborough, New Hampshire
name_zh: 新罕布什尔 · 彼得伯勒
prototype_of: 怀尔德在彼得伯勒的麦克道威尔艺术村写过《我们的小镇》的一部分，剧中的“格罗夫斯角”常被认为是照这座新英格兰小镇写的：几户人家、一座教堂、山坡上的墓地，生老病死都在这里。镇中心的砖楼和白色教堂仍是那个样子
prototype_of_en: Wilder wrote part of Our Town at the MacDowell Colony in Peterborough, and Grover's Corners is often said to be modelled on this New England town: a few families, a church, a cemetery on the hill, where people are born, marry and die. The brick buildings and white church of the town centre look much the same today

name: Monte Cristo Cottage, New London
name_zh: 新伦敦 · 基督山小屋
note: 奥尼尔一家每年夏天住在这座海边小屋，名字来自父亲一辈子演的《基督山伯爵》。《长夜漫漫路迢迢》写 1912 年夏天这一家人一天里的争吵和互相伤害：酗酒的父兄、吸毒的母亲、病中的儿子，几乎就是他自己的家。故居现为博物馆，客厅照剧本的舞台说明布置
note_en: The O'Neills spent every summer in this seaside cottage, named after The Count of Monte Cristo, the play the father acted in all his life. Long Day's Journey into Night follows one day of quarrels and wounds in the summer of 1912 — drinking father and brother, addicted mother, sick younger son — almost exactly his own family. The cottage is a museum, its living room arranged from the play's stage directions

name: Fleur-de-Lys Studios, Providence
name_zh: 普罗维登斯 · 鸢尾花工作室
note: 洛夫克拉夫特《克苏鲁的呼唤》里，年轻雕塑家威尔考克斯梦见沉没的城市后做出那块怪异的浅浮雕，他就住在托马斯街这座“鸢尾花大楼”里。洛夫克拉夫特把真实的楼名直接写进了小说。这座 1885 年的仿中世纪画室楼还在，就在第一浸信会教堂旁边的坡上
note_en: In The Call of Cthulhu, the young sculptor Wilcox makes his strange bas-relief after dreaming of a sunken city, and he lives in the 'Fleur-de-Lys Building' on Thomas Street; Lovecraft used the real name. The mock-medieval studio building of 1885 is still there, on the slope beside the First Baptist Church

name: Louisiana State Capitol, Baton Rouge
name_zh: 巴吞鲁日 · 路易斯安那州议会大厦
prototype_of: 沃伦《国王的人马》里的州长威利·斯塔克，原型是路易斯安那的平民主义州长休伊·朗。这座全美最高的州议会大厦就是朗主持修建的，1935 年他在大楼走廊里遇刺身亡，小说结尾斯塔克也在议会大厦里中枪。走廊墙上至今还能看到弹孔，朗就葬在楼前的花园里
prototype_of_en: Willie Stark, the governor in All the King's Men, is modelled on Louisiana's populist governor Huey Long. Long built this capitol, the tallest in the United States, and was shot dead in one of its corridors in 1935; Stark too is shot in the capitol at the end of the novel. Bullet marks can still be seen in the corridor wall, and Long is buried in the garden in front

name: Brooklyn Heights Promenade
name_zh: 布鲁克林 · 高地步道
note: 布鲁克林是好几部美国名作的家：《推销员之死》里威利·洛曼一家住在高楼包围中的布鲁克林小屋；《苏菲的抉择》里南方青年斯丁哥和集中营幸存者苏菲同住在弗拉特布什一座粉色公寓里；《卡瓦利与克雷》里逃出布拉格的乔就投奔布鲁克林的表弟。高地步道能望见整个曼哈顿下城
note_en: Brooklyn is home to several great American books: Willy Loman's family lives in a small Brooklyn house hemmed in by apartment blocks in Death of a Salesman; Stingo, a young Southerner, shares a pink boarding house in Flatbush with the camp survivor Sophie in Sophie's Choice; and Joe, escaping Prague in Kavalier & Clay, comes to his cousin in Brooklyn. The Heights Promenade looks across to lower Manhattan

name: Rebecca Nurse Homestead, Danvers
name_zh: 丹弗斯 · 丽贝卡·纳斯故居
note: 1692 年塞勒姆审巫案中，七十一岁的丽贝卡·纳斯被控行巫，在绞刑架上死去。阿瑟·米勒《萨勒姆的女巫》把她写成剧中最正直的人。她的农舍就在当年的塞勒姆村、今天的丹弗斯，屋旁的家族墓地里立着纪念碑，院里还有一座复原的塞勒姆村会堂
note_en: In the Salem witch trials of 1692, seventy-one-year-old Rebecca Nurse was accused of witchcraft and hanged. Arthur Miller made her the most upright figure in The Crucible. Her farmhouse stands in what was Salem Village, today Danvers, with a memorial in the family burying ground and a replica of the Salem Village meeting house on the grounds

name: Harlem, 125th Street
name_zh: 曼哈顿 · 哈莱姆 125 街
note: 哈莱姆是两部黑人文学经典的家：鲍德温生在这里，《向苍天呼吁》写一个哈莱姆少年在十四岁生日那天，在继父的小教堂里经历宗教上的“得救”；埃利森在这里写了七年《看不见的人》，无名的叙述者从南方来到哈莱姆，最后躲进地下室。125 街是哈莱姆的主街，阿波罗剧院就在这里
note_en: Harlem is home to two classics of Black American writing: Baldwin was born here, and Go Tell It on the Mountain follows a Harlem boy who is 'saved' in his stepfather's storefront church on his fourteenth birthday; Ellison spent seven years here writing Invisible Man, whose nameless narrator comes up from the South to Harlem and ends up hiding in a basement. 125th Street is Harlem's main street, home of the Apollo Theater
coord_checked: File:Apollo Theater Harlem NYC 2010.JPG (geotagged, Wikimedia Commons) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Apollo_Theater_Harlem_NYC_2010.JPG

name: Desolation Peak Lookout, North Cascades
name_zh: 北喀斯喀特 · 荒凉峰瞭望塔
note: 1956 年夏天，凯鲁亚克在北喀斯喀特山的荒凉峰顶当了六十三天山火瞭望员，一个人守着小木屋看云看山。《达摩流浪者》的结尾就写这段山上的日子，是他听了诗人朋友加里·斯奈德的建议上山的。木屋还在，徒步上去要一整天
note_en: In the summer of 1956 Kerouac spent sixty-three days alone as a fire lookout on top of Desolation Peak in the North Cascades, watching the clouds and mountains from a small cabin. The end of The Dharma Bums tells of those days on the mountain, which he took on at the urging of his poet friend Gary Snyder. The cabin still stands, a full day's hike up

name: Andalusia Farm, Milledgeville
name_zh: 米利奇维尔 · 安达卢西亚农场
note: 奥康纳二十五岁时确诊红斑狼疮，从此和母亲住在佐治亚中部这座农场，养了几十只孔雀，每天上午写作三小时，直到 1964 年去世。《智血》的定稿和她大部分短篇都写在这里。农场现由佐治亚学院管理开放，她的卧室兼书房原样保留，院子里又养起了孔雀
note_en: Diagnosed with lupus at twenty-five, O'Connor lived on this middle-Georgia farm with her mother from then on, kept dozens of peacocks, and wrote three hours every morning until she died in 1964. She finished Wise Blood and wrote most of her stories here. The farm is open to visitors under Georgia College; her bedroom-study is kept as it was, and peacocks are back in the yard

name: Lorain, Ohio
note: 莫里森生在伊利湖边这座钢铁小城，她的第一部小说《最蓝的眼睛》就写 1941 年的洛雷恩：一个黑人小女孩每天祈祷自己有一双蓝眼睛。镇上的公共图书馆有一间以莫里森命名的阅览室，湖边还是当年的钢厂和船坞
note_en: Morrison was born in this steel town on Lake Erie, and her first novel, The Bluest Eye, is set in Lorain in 1941, where a little Black girl prays every day for blue eyes. The public library has a reading room named after Morrison, and the steel mill and docks still line the lake

name: Aldo Leopold Shack, Baraboo
name_zh: 巴拉布 · 利奥波德小屋
note: 1935 年利奥波德在威斯康星河边买下一片被耗尽的农场，把唯一剩下的鸡舍改成小屋，一家人周末来这里种了几千棵松树。《沙乡年鉴》按月份记下这片地上的花鸟和季节，提出了“土地伦理”。小屋和他们种的松林都还在，由利奥波德基金会带人参观
note_en: In 1935 Leopold bought a worn-out farm on the Wisconsin River, turned its only remaining building, a chicken coop, into a cabin, and the family came on weekends to plant thousands of pines. A Sand County Almanac records the birds, flowers and seasons of this land month by month and sets out his 'land ethic.' The shack and the pines they planted are still there, with tours by the Leopold Foundation

name: Downtown Albany
name_zh: 纽约州 · 奥尔巴尼老城
note: 肯尼迪的“奥尔巴尼三部曲”都写他的家乡。《紫苑草》里，1938 年万圣节前后，当年的棒球手弗朗西斯·费伦流浪回奥尔巴尼，在墓地给人挖坟，一边被鬼魂纠缠，一边想回到抛下二十二年的家。州政府大楼和老城区的街道今天还是小说里的样子
note_en: All of William Kennedy's Albany novels are set in his home town. In Ironweed, around Halloween 1938, Francis Phelan, once a ballplayer, drifts back to Albany, digs graves in the cemetery, is haunted by ghosts, and tries to return to the family he left twenty-two years before. The state capitol and the old downtown streets still look much as they do in the book

name: National Underground Railroad Freedom Center, Cincinnati
name_zh: 辛辛那提 · 地下铁道自由中心
note: 辛辛那提隔着俄亥俄河就是蓄奴的肯塔基，很多逃亡者从这里踏上自由州。1856 年玛格丽特·加纳带着孩子逃到这里，追捕者赶到时她杀死了自己的女儿，莫里森据此写成《宠儿》，故事就发生在城外。河边的自由中心讲地下铁道的历史，怀特黑德在《地下铁道》里把这条秘密通道想象成了真的铁路
note_en: Across the Ohio River from Cincinnati lay slaveholding Kentucky, and many fugitives first touched free soil here. In 1856 Margaret Garner fled here with her children and killed her daughter when the slave catchers came; Morrison made her story into Beloved, set just outside the city. The Freedom Center on the riverbank tells the history of the Underground Railroad, which Colson Whitehead reimagined as a real railroad
coord_checked: National Underground Railroad Freedom Center (Wikimedia Commons) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Category:National_Underground_Railroad_Freedom_Center

name: Turtle Mountain Reservation, North Dakota
name_zh: 北达科他 · 龟山保留地
prototype_of: 厄德里克是龟山奇佩瓦部落的登记成员，外祖父当过部落主席。《爱药》《圆屋》写北达科他一个奇佩瓦保留地上几个家族几十年的故事，这个保留地很像龟山。《圆屋》里十三岁的乔为遭到侵害的母亲寻找真相。保留地在加拿大边境旁的丘陵湖泊之间
prototype_of_en: Erdrich is an enrolled member of the Turtle Mountain Band of Chippewa, and her grandfather was its tribal chairman. Love Medicine and The Round House follow several families over decades on an Ojibwe reservation in North Dakota much like Turtle Mountain; in The Round House thirteen-year-old Joe searches for the truth after his mother is attacked. The reservation lies among hills and lakes by the Canadian border

name: San Angelo, Texas
name_zh: 得克萨斯 · 圣安杰洛
note: 麦卡锡《天下骏马》开篇在 1949 年的圣安杰洛一带：外祖父去世，十六岁的约翰·格雷迪眼看家里的牧场要被卖掉，就和朋友骑马南下，越过边境去墨西哥找属于牛仔的生活。这座西得克萨斯小城至今还是牧场和牛仔竞技的中心
note_en: All the Pretty Horses opens around San Angelo in 1949: his grandfather dead and the family ranch about to be sold, sixteen-year-old John Grady Cole rides south with a friend across the border into Mexico in search of a cowboy's life. This West Texas town is still a centre of ranching and rodeo

name: Knoxville, Tennessee
name_zh: 田纳西 · 诺克斯维尔
note: 麦卡锡在诺克斯维尔长大，早期小说《沙崔》就写这座城。《长路》里没有一个地名，父子推着购物车穿过一片烧焦的大地往南走向大海，许多读者从山路、桥和河认出了他熟悉的东田纳西。诺克斯维尔老城有麦卡锡长大的街区，田纳西河从城中流过
note_en: McCarthy grew up in Knoxville, and his early novel Suttree is set here. The Road names no places at all — a father and son push a shopping cart south through a burned land toward the sea — but many readers recognise the mountain roads, bridges and rivers of the East Tennessee he knew. The Tennessee River runs through the city

name: Bennington College, Vermont
name_zh: 佛蒙特 · 本宁顿学院
prototype_of: 塔特《校园秘史》里那所佛蒙特小学院“汉普登”，一般认为照的是她自己念过的本宁顿学院：一小群学古希腊文的学生，在山间校园里杀了自己的同学。本宁顿以艺术和写作出名，同时期的同学里还有作家布雷特·伊斯顿·埃利斯。校园在小镇外的山坡草地上
prototype_of_en: Hampden, the small Vermont college of The Secret History, is generally taken to be Bennington, where Tartt studied: a small circle of students of ancient Greek murder one of their own on a hillside campus. Bennington is known for the arts and writing, and Bret Easton Ellis was a fellow student. The campus spreads over meadows on a hill outside town

name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
name_zh: 曼哈顿 · 大都会艺术博物馆
note: 塔特《金翅雀》开篇，十三岁的西奥和母亲在大都会博物馆看画，一场爆炸夺走了母亲，他在废墟中拿走了法布里蒂乌斯的小画《金翅雀》，从此带着它过了十几年。那幅画真迹在海牙的莫瑞泰斯皇家美术馆。博物馆的大台阶是纽约人约见的地方
note_en: The Goldfinch opens with thirteen-year-old Theo and his mother looking at paintings in the Met when a bomb goes off; his mother is killed, and from the rubble he takes Fabritius's small painting The Goldfinch and carries it for more than a decade. The real painting hangs in the Mauritshuis in The Hague. The museum's great steps are where New Yorkers meet

name: Detroit
note: 两部小说都写底特律的汽车工厂：塞利纳《茫茫黑夜漫游》里，巴尔达穆从纽约来到底特律，在福特的流水线上做工，觉得人被机器吞掉；尤金尼德斯《中性》里，希腊移民祖父也在福特厂里谋生，一家人后来搬到格罗斯波因特的米德尔塞克斯大道。底特律是福特发家的城市
note_en: Two novels go into Detroit's car plants: in Céline's Journey to the End of the Night, Bardamu comes from New York to work on Ford's assembly line and feels swallowed by the machines; in Eugenides's Middlesex, the Greek immigrant grandfather finds work at Ford too, and the family later moves to Middlesex Boulevard in Grosse Pointe. Detroit is the city where Ford began

name: Great Falls of the Passaic, Paterson
name_zh: 帕特森 · 帕塞伊克大瀑布
note: 迪亚斯《奥斯卡·瓦奥短暂而奇妙的一生》里，胖胖的多米尼加裔书呆子奥斯卡在新泽西的帕特森长大，读科幻、玩桌游，一心想谈恋爱。帕特森是美国早期的工业城市，靠的就是城中这道瀑布的水力，诗人威廉斯也写过一部长诗《帕特森》。瀑布现属国家历史公园
note_en: In The Brief Wondrous Life of Oscar Wao, Oscar, an overweight Dominican nerd who reads science fiction, plays role-playing games and longs for love, grows up in Paterson, New Jersey. Paterson was one of America's first industrial cities, powered by these falls, and William Carlos Williams wrote a long poem named after it. The falls are now a national historical park

name: Indian Springs School, Alabama
name_zh: 亚拉巴马 · 印第安斯普林斯学校
prototype_of: 约翰·格林念过伯明翰郊外这所寄宿学校，《寻找阿拉斯加》里的卡尔弗溪寄宿学校就是照它写的：迈尔斯转学到这里寻找“伟大的或许”，遇见了神秘的女孩阿拉斯加。校园在伯明翰南边的树林里，有一片湖
prototype_of_en: John Green attended this boarding school outside Birmingham, and Culver Creek in Looking for Alaska is based on it: Miles transfers here in search of a 'Great Perhaps' and meets the enigmatic Alaska Young. The campus lies in the woods south of Birmingham, around a lake

name: North Carolina coastal marshes
note: 欧文斯《蝲蛄吟唱的地方》里，被家人一个个抛下的女孩凯娅独自在北卡罗来纳海边的沼泽里长大，被镇上人叫作“沼泽女孩”。小说里的巴克利湾小镇是虚构的。北卡罗来纳的外滩群岛一带有大片盐沼、潮汐河道和水鸟，正是书里那样的风景
note_en: In Where the Crawdads Sing, Kya, abandoned by her family one by one, grows up alone in the marshes of the North Carolina coast, where the townspeople call her 'the Marsh Girl.' The town of Barkley Cove is fictional. The Outer Banks of North Carolina have wide salt marshes, tidal creeks and water birds, the landscape of the book

name: Dozier School for Boys, Marianna
name_zh: 玛丽安娜 · 多齐尔男校旧址
prototype_of: 怀特黑德《黑人男孩》里的“尼克尔学院”原型是佛罗里达的这所少年感化院，1900 年到 2011 年关闭，一百多年里有大量男孩遭到毒打，2012 年起考古学家在校园里挖出了五十多具无名遗骸。小说里埃尔伍德因为搭错一趟车被送进这里。旧址现已荒废
prototype_of_en: The Nickel Academy of The Nickel Boys is based on this Florida reform school, open from 1900 until 2011, where generations of boys were brutally beaten; from 2012 archaeologists dug up more than fifty unmarked graves on the grounds. In the novel Elwood is sent here after accepting the wrong ride. The site is now abandoned

name: Mississippi State Penitentiary (Parchman Farm)
name_zh: 密西西比州立监狱（帕奇曼农场）
note: 沃德《歌唱吧，未安葬的魂灵》里，母亲莉奥妮带着两个孩子开车穿过密西西比，去帕奇曼监狱接出狱的丈夫，外祖父年轻时也被关在这里，一个死在这里的黑人少年的鬼魂跟着他们回家。帕奇曼建在三角洲的棉田里，曾是南方最残酷的劳役监狱
note_en: In Sing, Unburied, Sing, Leonie drives her two children across Mississippi to collect her husband from Parchman; their grandfather was held here as a young man, and the ghost of a Black boy who died here follows them home. Parchman sits among Delta cotton fields and was once the harshest labour prison in the South

name: Lee County, Virginia
note: 金索沃把狄更斯的《大卫·科波菲尔》搬到弗吉尼亚最西端的李县：主人公“恶魔”在阿巴拉契亚山区的单宽活动房里出生，经历寄养、童工、橄榄球和止痛药成瘾的浪潮。金索沃自己在肯塔基乡下长大，熟悉这片山区。县里是连绵的山岭和煤矿小镇
note_en: Kingsolver moved Dickens's David Copperfield to Lee County, at the far western tip of Virginia: her hero 'Demon' is born in a single-wide trailer in the Appalachian mountains and lives through foster care, child labour, football and the opioid epidemic. Kingsolver herself grew up in rural Kentucky and knows these mountains. The county is ridges and old coal towns

name: Boulder, Colorado
note: 斯蒂芬·金《末日逼近》里，一场瘟疫杀死了几乎所有人，幸存者分成两边：好人跟着一百零八岁的阿巴盖尔大妈聚到博尔德，建起“博尔德自由区”，坏人投奔拉斯维加斯。金写这本书时就住在博尔德。城边是熨斗山的红色岩壁
note_en: In Stephen King's The Stand a plague kills almost everyone and the survivors divide: the good gather around 108-year-old Mother Abagail in Boulder to found the 'Boulder Free Zone,' the evil go to Las Vegas. King lived in Boulder while writing it. The red rock slabs of the Flatirons rise at the edge of town

name: The Stanley Hotel, Estes Park
name_zh: 埃斯蒂斯帕克 · 斯坦利酒店
prototype_of: 1974 年斯蒂芬·金和妻子在落基山脚下这家酒店住了一晚，正赶上停业前夕，偌大的酒店只有他们两个客人，他住的是 217 号房。这一夜给了他《闪灵》里远望酒店的灵感。酒店至今营业，217 号房常被预订，还有专门的“鬼魂导览”
prototype_of_en: In 1974 Stephen King and his wife spent a night in this hotel at the foot of the Rockies just before it closed for the season, the only guests in the whole building; he stayed in room 217. That night gave him the Overlook Hotel of The Shining. The hotel is still open, room 217 is much in demand, and there are ghost tours

name: Cairo, Illinois
prototype_of: 狄更斯 1842 年游美国时坐船经过密西西比河和俄亥俄河交汇处的开罗，觉得这片低洼泥沼是他见过最凄惨的地方。《马丁·瞿述伟》里，马丁被骗买下“伊甸”殖民地的地，到了才发现是一片疫病横行的沼泽，一般认为写的就是开罗。小城今天人口已很稀少，老街上多是空楼
prototype_of_en: On his American tour of 1842 Dickens passed Cairo, where the Ohio meets the Mississippi, and thought the low swamp the most dismal place he had seen. In Martin Chuzzlewit, Martin is swindled into buying land in the settlement of 'Eden' and finds a fever-ridden swamp, generally taken to be Cairo. The town is much emptier now, its old streets lined with vacant buildings

name: House on the Rock, Spring Green
name_zh: 斯普林格林 · 岩上之屋
note: 盖曼《美国众神》里，奥丁化身的星期三先生把各路古老神祇召集到威斯康星的岩上之屋，在世界最大的旋转木马上把他们带进神的国度。这座建在岩柱上的奇屋是亚历克斯·乔丹一手造的，堆满了自动乐器、怪诞收藏和一个伸出山崖的“无限房间”
note_en: In Gaiman's American Gods, Mr. Wednesday — Odin in disguise — summons the old gods to the House on the Rock in Wisconsin and carries them off to the realm of the gods on the world's largest carousel. Alex Jordan built this strange house on a rock pillar, crammed with mechanical music machines, bizarre collections and an 'Infinity Room' jutting out over the valley

name: Dyea, Alaska
note: 《野性的呼唤》第二章，被偷卖的大狗巴克在戴伊的海滩上第一次见识北方的规矩：同伴被狗群撕碎，他被套上雪橇。1897 年淘金潮时，杰克·伦敦本人也在这里上岸，背着行李翻过奇尔库特山口去育空。戴伊如今只剩树林里的墓地和码头残桩，奇尔库特步道的起点就在这里
note_en: In chapter two of The Call of the Wild, Buck, stolen and sold north, learns the law of the North on the beach at Dyea, where a dog is torn apart and he is put in harness. In the gold rush of 1897 Jack London himself landed here and packed his gear over the Chilkoot Pass to the Yukon. Dyea is now just a cemetery in the woods and the stumps of a wharf, at the start of the Chilkoot Trail

name: Elysian Fields Avenue, Faubourg Marigny, New Orleans
name_zh: 新奥尔良 · 极乐世界大道
note: 《欲望号街车》开场，布兰奇按妹妹斯黛拉给的指路，先坐“欲望”号街车，再换乘“墓地”号，在“极乐世界”下车，来到斯坦利和斯黛拉在法国区边上的两居室。这条大道真实存在，从密西西比河边一直通到庞恰特雷恩湖。威廉斯写这部剧时就住在附近
note_en: At the start of A Streetcar Named Desire, Blanche follows her sister's directions: take a streetcar named Desire, transfer to one called Cemeteries, and get off at Elysian Fields — the street of Stanley and Stella's two-room flat at the edge of the French Quarter. The avenue is real, running from the Mississippi to Lake Pontchartrain. Williams lived nearby while writing the play

name: Gentilly, New Orleans
note: 珀西《看电影的人》的主人公宾克斯是新奥尔良的股票经纪人，住在中产郊区让蒂伊，靠看电影打发日子，在狂欢节前的一周里开始“寻找”。他特意离开花园区的老家族圈子，搬到这片平淡的新住宅区。让蒂伊在城北，靠近庞恰特雷恩湖
note_en: Binx Bolling, The Moviegoer's hero, is a New Orleans stockbroker who lives in the middle-class suburb of Gentilly, passes his days at the movies, and in the week before Mardi Gras sets out on a 'search.' He has deliberately left his old family circle in the Garden District for these plain new houses. Gentilly lies on the north side of the city near Lake Pontchartrain

name: Kurt Vonnegut Museum and Library, Indianapolis
name_zh: 印第安纳波利斯 · 冯内古特博物馆
note: 冯内古特生在印第安纳波利斯。二战时他作为战俘在德累斯顿的屠宰场地下室里躲过了盟军大轰炸，二十多年后写成《五号屠场》，主人公比利“在时间里脱了节”。故乡的博物馆陈列他的打字机、画作和战俘时期的经历，还有一间“被禁书”展室
note_en: Vonnegut was born in Indianapolis. As a prisoner of war he survived the Allied firebombing of Dresden in the cellar of a slaughterhouse, and more than twenty years later wrote Slaughterhouse-Five, whose hero Billy Pilgrim 'has come unstuck in time.' The museum in his home town shows his typewriter, drawings and his wartime experience, with a room on banned books
coord_checked: Kurt Vonnegut Museum and Library (Wikimedia Commons) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Category:Kurt_Vonnegut_Museum_and_Library

name: Beale Street, Memphis
note: 赖特在自传《黑孩子》里写，十七岁时他从密西西比来到孟菲斯，住在比尔街附近，做杂役攒钱，借白人同事的图书证偷偷去图书馆借门肯的书，从此决心当作家，再一路北上芝加哥。比尔街是布鲁斯音乐的发源地之一，今天满街是酒吧和音乐现场
note_en: In Black Boy, Wright tells how at seventeen he came up from Mississippi to Memphis, lodged near Beale Street, saved his wages from odd jobs, and borrowed a white co-worker's library card to read H. L. Mencken — the moment he decided to be a writer before heading north to Chicago. Beale Street is one of the birthplaces of the blues and is full of bars and live music today

name: Bronzeville, Chicago
name_zh: 芝加哥 · 布朗兹维尔
note: 《土生子》里的比格·托马斯一家挤在芝加哥南区一间爬满老鼠的单间公寓里，他去给富人家当司机，失手杀死了主人的女儿。南区的布朗兹维尔是黑人大迁徙后形成的“城中之城”，赖特 1927 年到芝加哥后就住在这一带。街区里还有很多当年的老楼
note_en: Native Son's Bigger Thomas lives with his family in a rat-infested one-room flat on Chicago's South Side, takes a job as a rich family's chauffeur and accidentally kills their daughter. Bronzeville on the South Side became a 'city within a city' after the Great Migration, and Wright lived around here after reaching Chicago in 1927. Many of the old buildings still stand
coord_checked: File:22 121278 YMCA from el, Bronzeville Chicago.jpg (geotagged, Wikimedia Commons) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:22_121278_YMCA_from_el,_Bronzeville_Chicago.jpg

name: Humboldt Park, Chicago
note: “我是美国人，生在芝加哥。”贝娄《奥吉·马奇历险记》这样开头，奥吉就在西北区洪堡公园一带的穷人家长大，贝娄自己少年时也住在这里。他后来的《洪堡的礼物》写芝加哥的作家和他那位落魄诗人朋友洪堡。公园里有湖、船屋和老式的花园
note_en: 'I am an American, Chicago born' — so begins The Adventures of Augie March, whose hero grows up poor around Humboldt Park on the Northwest Side, where Bellow himself lived as a boy. His later Humboldt's Gift follows a Chicago writer and his ruined poet friend Humboldt. The park has a lagoon, a boathouse and old formal gardens

name: Tennessee Williams's home, Westminster Place, St. Louis
name_zh: 圣路易斯 · 威斯敏斯特街威廉斯旧居
prototype_of: 《玻璃动物园》是田纳西·威廉斯的“回忆剧”，温菲尔德一家住在圣路易斯一座小巷里的公寓，照的就是他少年时和母亲、姐姐住过的这一带公寓，姐姐罗丝正是剧中摆弄玻璃动物的劳拉的原型。威斯敏斯特街这座公寓楼至今还在，是私人住宅
prototype_of_en: The Glass Menagerie is Williams's 'memory play.' The Wingfields' alley apartment in St. Louis is modelled on the apartment where he lived as a youth with his mother and his sister Rose, the model for Laura with her glass animals. The building on Westminster Place still stands as private flats

name: Compo Beach, Westport
name_zh: 韦斯特波特 · 康波海滩
note: 1920 年 5 月，刚结婚的菲茨杰拉德夫妇从纽约搬到康涅狄格的韦斯特波特，在康波海滩附近租了一座小屋过夏天，派对不断，有一回客人恶作剧拉响了火警。《美丽与毁灭》写一对挥霍青春、坐等遗产的纽约夫妻，在城里公寓和乡下房子之间来回，有很多这段日子的影子。海滩至今是镇上夏天最热闹的地方
note_en: In May 1920 the newly married Fitzgeralds moved from New York to Westport, Connecticut, and rented a cottage near Compo Beach for the summer; the parties never stopped, and once a guest pulled the fire alarm as a prank. The Beautiful and Damned, about a New York couple squandering their youth while waiting for an inheritance, shuttling between a city apartment and a country house, carries much of that summer. The beach is still the liveliest place in town in summer
